messages.author: 55cb20da3fe82e18
messages.subject: downloadHandler example for pdf
parts:
This maybe trivial, but is there a quick example on how to use downloadHandler to write/save pdf content? I've always used the pdf function which takes a file name (not a connection) - similarly savePlot takes a file name. The example in the documentation uses write.csv which takes both file names or connections. I haven't found something similar for saving pdf files

Also curious if using downloadHandler is superior to my simple implementation:

in server.R:

  getplot <- reactive(function()
  {
      ...
      pdf(file=outputFile,width=12,height=16)
      grid.arrange(result[[1]], result[[2]])
      dev.off()
      ...
  }
  ....

  output$plotpdf <- reactiveUI(function()
  {
    temp = getplot()
    a(href=outputFile, 'Download Plot PDF')      
  }

and then I just call htmlOutput('plotpdf') in the UI

Is downloadHandler doing something equivalent in the background?

 
Thanks

-Haider

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: downloadHandler example for pdf
parts:
Hmmm, I didn't realize there were commonly used functions in R that only took filenames. That is a bummer. I think the easiest workaround would be to write to a tempfile, then transfer the contents to the connection you're given.

output$plotpdf <- downloadHandler(
  filename = 'plot.pdf',
  content = function(con) {
    temp <- tempfile()
    on.exit(unlink(temp))
    pdf(file=temp, ...)
    ...
    dev.off()
    bytes <- readBin(temp, "raw", file.info(temp)$size)
    writeBin(bytes, con)
  }
)

Does your simple implementation actually work? Oh, is the outputFile a path that's inside the www directory or something?

One advantage of using downloadHandler is that no expense is incurred unless the user actually clicks the download link; the `content` function is not invoked until the content is actually needed. This isn't the case with your reactiveUI approach, where the PDF is regenerated and pushed down to the browser every time, just in case the user does click the link.

Maybe I should revise the downloadHandler content function to take a filename instead... or, either...

messages.subject: Re: downloadHandler example for pdf
parts: Does your simple implementation actually work? Oh, is the outputFile a path that's inside the www directory or something?

Yup it works - I write the file in to a www directory and then it's available. I'm okay with the pre-generated file vs on the fly trade-off - my plots are sort of big and complicated and I like the real-time feel of getting the resulting file if needed. 

Sort of tangential issue/concern that I've noticed: my plotting is wrapped in a reactive function so that it doesn't have to be called multiple times but is inside a tabPanel. However, every time you click away from the plot tab to another tab and back, it takes a noticeable amount of time to re-draw the plot (seems like it writes it to the graphics device every time). Is that the intended behavior? Is there any way to prevent this? It would make sense that everything is cached if I'm just cycling through the different tabPanels looking at different views of my data (i.e. one tab has summary stats, another has the plot, etc) and the inputs have not changed at all.

Thanks

-Haider

However, every time you click away from the plot tab to another tab and back, it takes a noticeable amount of time to re-draw the plot (seems like it writes it to the graphics device every time). Is that the intended behavior? Is there any way to prevent this? It would make sense that everything is cached if I'm just cycling through the different tabPanels looking at different views of my data (i.e. one tab has summary stats, another has the plot, etc) and the inputs have not changed at all.

Does this behavior stop if you give reactivePlot explicit width and height values? If so, it's because Shiny has noticed that the plot "size" changed as you flipped between tabs. This may seem like a misfeature, but it allows a different kind of optimization: plots on hidden tabs can be skipped automatically (although this isn't true if you give explicit width and height).
